MIND-177: Add a CI flake reconciler that turns Minds flaky tests into MIND Linear tickets, ported from Sculptor's SCU-534 flaky-test reporter and re-engineered so the clustering is done by the invoking agent rather than by brittle string rules.

New `scripts/flake_reconcile.py` is a thin data-access + Linear-mutation CLI, always driven by the flake skills (`detect-flakes`, `manage-flakes`, `report-incidental-flakes`). It deliberately does NOT root-cause or cluster failures. Subcommands: `list-flakes` reads the `report-flaky-aware-tests` check-run summaries over a window (via `gh`) and prints, as JSON, each test that flaky-recovered at least once (so branch gates like ruff/type/docs are excluded) along with its distinct failure messages, flaking/hard-fail commit counts, `@pytest.mark.flaky` status, and window bounds; `list-tickets` prints the team's existing `flaky-cluster` tickets verbatim (body included); `create-ticket`, `update-ticket`, and `close-ticket` mutate Linear (bodies passed via `--body-file`). Linear access goes through `latchkey`; the `flaky-cluster` label is auto-created if missing.

The judgment lives in three composable skills under `.claude/skills/`. **`manage-flakes`** is the reusable core: given a set of flaky tests, the agent reads the failure text and clusters them **for resolution** -- each ticket a handoff unit one future agent can fix as a single coherent effort, grouped by root cause rather than shared symptom (the guidance refuses the "defensibility / inertia" failure mode and splits when a grouping bundles unrelated fixes). It embeds a stable `flake-cluster` marker plus a `last-seen` timestamp to dedup on later runs, reconciles against existing tickets (create / update / recluster), and prioritizes by a deterministic **branch filter**: a cluster whose flakes were seen on `main`, or on more than one feature branch, is filed "ready to work on" (the first unstarted state, e.g. Todo); one only ever seen on a single unmerged feature branch is filed to backlog, since it is most likely that branch's own bug and a fixer could not reproduce it on `main`. It changes a ticket's state only while still in a pre-work state, never rewrites a human or agent move (In Progress / In Review / Done / Canceled), and comments on any change; closing a cluster as stale (unseen for 21 days) is allowed only on a full-window sweep. **`detect-flakes`** is the batch entry -- it sweeps CI over a window and hands the full set to `manage-flakes`. **`report-incidental-flakes`** is a best-effort entry for a coding/babysitting agent that just hit a flake: it verifies Linear access (degrading, when absent, to just highlighting the flake and marking the test `@pytest.mark.flaky`), confirms the failing test pre-exists on `main` and is not attributable to the branch's own new code, then hands the single flake to `manage-flakes` in create/update-only mode. New CLI subcommands back all this: `preferred-status`, `set-status`, `comment-ticket`, and `update-ticket --title` for in-place re-scoping. The read subcommands are side-effect-free; nothing is written until the agent shows a plan, gets approval, and runs the mutating subcommands.

New `.claude/skills/deflake-mngr-ci/SKILL.md` is the fixing counterpart to the flake-detection skills: invoked as `/deflake-mngr-ci <ticket>`, it drives a single filed flake ticket from adoption through a principled fix to a draft PR. It orchestrates the existing `work-on-linear`, `de-complect`, and `crispy-comments` skills (referencing rather than restating them) and insists on finding the true root cause, splitting a ticket that turns out to be several bugs, rejecting band-aid fixes (blind timeout bumps, error special-casing) in favor of changes that improve the repo long-term, and escalating genuine design tradeoffs to a human. The skill is written to be rot-resistant: it points to the sibling skills, the ticket format, and the repo's own conventions rather than duplicating them. The `work-on-linear` skill it orchestrates is now vendored into the repo at `.claude/skills/work-on-linear/` (a sibling of `crispy-comments`), so it ships and versions with the repo instead of relying on a user's global skill library.
